Stop calling this "faceless". If you're not voicing or even scripting then this is not the same as someone who writes and voices their content but chooses not to appear on camera.

Camera makes it personal but even if you want to go faceless, it will probably work out as long as your commentary/storytelling is good. I would highly recommend that you study MrBeast's videos and learn how he builds curiosity with open loops.

The model exists, and it works well for a goal that is probably not yours.

When independent clippers post to their own accounts, the views and the followers land on those accounts. That is genuinely useful if the thing you sell lives off platform, like a course, or a name people search for once they have heard it. It does much less for your channel, because the viewer never arrives at you. They arrive at a faceless account that happens to feature you.

If growing your own channel is the point, the version that works is clips on your own accounts, and then the whole game is selection rather than volume. One clip that stands on its own beats twenty cut on a punchy line that only makes sense to someone who already watched the episode.

On the control question, the thing creators underestimate is framing. A clipper paid on views optimises for whatever travels, and that is usually the most inflammatory 30 seconds you said all year with the sentence before it removed. You would be handing that decision to someone whose incentive is not your reputation.

For a faceless IG account, the biggest win early is having a repeatable Reels script template so you’re not reinventing every post.

A simple structure that usually holds attention:

• 0–1s: very specific promise (“3 signs your nervous system is overloaded after birth…”)

• 1–10s: deliver 1 concrete point fast (no long intro)

• 10–25s: 2nd point + example

• 25–35s: 3rd point + what to do next

• Last 2s: CTA to a series (“Part 2 tomorrow: what helped me most…”) to drive follows

good luck!

“Faceless” is a production choice, not a niche. Reddit stories over Minecraft parkour are easy to produce precisely because thousands of channels can make the same thing, and lightly repackaged stories can create originality and monetisation problems.

If you want to stay off camera, build the value somewhere else: original reporting, your own stories, a distinctive narrator, research, animation, or a format people can identify without seeing your face. Make ten cheap pilots before buying tools or outsourcing anything.

If the only advantage is that the videos are fast to manufacture, I would choose a different side hustle.
